newsitem.title: PERU: Peru makes gasoline tax independent of intl prices.
newsitem.headline: Peru makes gasoline tax independent of intl prices.

text.p: Peru's government lowered by 30 percent its "selective" tax on industrial gasoline that should result in a 10 percent price reduction for the consumer, the state's daily El Peruano said Wednesday.

The reduction is due to a new formula for calculating tax on industrial gasoline that eliminates the correlation between international prices and the levy paid to the state treasury, the government said.

"From now on, when international gasoline prices vary, there will be no change to the tax levy because it is fixed in the (local) sol currency," economist Armando Zolezzi told local redio Radioprogramas del Peru, explaining the new decree.

Last December, the government said it was concerned private companies were hiking gasoline prices due to rising prices on international markets. The price hikes provoked widespread protest in Peru and prompted the government to put on hold its ongoing, piecemeal privatization of its oil assets.
